subject: biology
title: Organisation Adventure
welcome_lead: From a single cell up to a whole organism — meet the levels of life.
meta_desc: GCSE Biology Organisation walkthrough — cell to tissue to organ to organ system, plus human and plant tissue examples.
final_note: You learned the levels of organisation, named four human tissues (epithelial, muscle, glandular, connective), and four plant tissues (epidermal, mesophyll, xylem, phloem).

concepts.def: Group of similar cells doing the same job
Group of tissues working together (e.g. stomach)
Lines and covers surfaces of the body
Plant tissue — carries water and minerals up
Plant tissue — carries dissolved sugars around

walkthroughs.body_html:
Cell → Tissue → Organ → Organ system → Organism

- A cell is the basic unit.
- A tissue is many similar cells doing the same job.
- An organ is several tissues working together.
- An organ system is several organs working together.
- The whole organism is all the systems combined.

Four to know:

- Epithelial — lines surfaces (gut, lungs, skin).
- Muscle — contracts to make movement.
- Glandular — makes and releases secretions like enzymes or hormones.
- Connective — holds things together (bone, cartilage, blood).

The stomach is a great example — it has all four.

Plants are organised too. A leaf is an organ. Inside it:

- Epidermal tissue — covers the leaf (with a waxy cuticle).
- Palisade mesophyll — packed with chloroplasts for photosynthesis.
- Xylem — carries water up from the roots.
- Phloem — carries dissolved sugars around the plant.

numericals.q: A stomach contains epithelial, muscle, glandular and connective tissue. How many DIFFERENT tissue types is that?
numericals.hint: Count the tissues in the list.
